attempts.title: About Time — official publisher Mini Rules and dated game-elements/token clarification reference
attempts.selection_note: Official publisher Mini Rules posted November 2012 by co-designer Joe Gill, successfully retrieved unchanged from its actual December 2012 public capture. This is the named Circa Circa historical-year guessing game, matching BGG 32337 and the local character/cardholder/TimeCard/token/centre mechanics, not unrelated clock-learning games. The archive requested through the older plural domain redirected to the actual singular abouttimeboardgame.com publisher site; its bounded historical index and linked pages supplied this primary reference, where the earlier plural-domain PDF-only search had not. The complete Mini Rules article was read, with complete selected 2010 primary game-elements page and signed 2010 token clarification as separately labelled supporting text. Together they provide character-at-Start setup, four initial TimeCards, initial one-token pot/no tokens distributed to players, youngest first, colour/category question, all-team 30-second written year guesses except Duels, answer reveal, nearest-year reward, exact-answer doubling, winner becoming next Reader and moving, first Time shout, Reader exclusion, five-token centre round, failed-centre return to Castle and most-tokens victory. The 2010 game-elements page supplies category/component use, Duel half-token transfer rounded down and Plague half-token pot effect. Accurate source type is publisher RULES REFERENCE HTML, not a recovered full printed rulebook, all original 2007/2008 pages or complete component deck. The Mini Rules explicitly refers to unavailable rulebook page 4 for full tied-round Rollover handling. All Highwayman/board-space details, every TimeCard and complete question-card/timeline components are not recovered or certified. The 2010 token clarification explicitly concerns the 2008 UK edition, while the 2012 Mini Rules is later publisher core guidance; texts remain dated and separate rather than silently declaring every edition identical. Its exchange sentence self-references tokens marked 10; this original textual ambiguity is retained verbatim, not used to invent a denomination-exchange procedure. Selected HTML excludes navigation/reviews, preserves source wording and normalizes only whitespace/line wrapping; all three unchanged originals and hashes remain available. Old playabouttime.com HTML was statically inspected but provided marketing/Flash-host text, not the missing full rules; no Flash was executed. One specific MAJOR Reader/TimeCard eligibility finding is recorded against the covered publisher Mini Rules; no complete summary audit, PASS or body repair.

It combines typeset shared rules with scans of all eight original ship hit records and special-weapon sheets (Dort,Earthship,Kuzi,Repazoid,Rojun,Rux,Zark,Zeron),ship counters,templates and weapon-interaction chart. All eight ship-record/weapon pairs and final template/cross-index coverage were checked; Dort weapon sheet and full cross-index were visually read. Not every individual special-weapon interaction was independently audited. attempts.title: BattleTroops — original FASA1989 manual,45scanned pages; fresh English OCR
attempts.selection_note: Original FASA1989 BattleTroops manual,45scanned PDF pages, successfully retrieved from the public BattleTech[multi]/Sourcebooks/FASA directory under its actual FASA1637 filename. This deeper Sourcebooks branch is distinct from the previously inspected Core/FASA/EXTRA branches; it is not ClanTroops, generic BattleTech tactical rules or the old Dragon magazine advertisement. Original front cover, contents and credits/copyright pages identify BattleTroops urban man-to-man combat in the BattleTech universe, Sam Lewis/Jordan Weisman/L.RossBabcockIII and FASA1989. Basic/core text PDF4–18 and all three scenario texts PDF36–39 were read in fresh OCR. Original pages1–3,7–9,14,36and39 were visually inspected, including exact activation sequence and conflicting hand-to-hand costs. Book contains components/dot maps/records/setup, first-turn initiative, side-complete movement and reactive immediate combat, terrain/MP/firing arcs/LOS, ranged/melee/damage/lethal-versus-bruise, grenades/armor, optional weapons/leadership/morale/MechWarrior/BattleTech/vehicles/mines/fire, platoon organization, three scenarios and record/reference/template pages. All45pages received fresh forced English OCR because every original native text page was empty. OCR has table/diagram/record-sheet and typography errors, with low text on template pages and blank decorative/back page. Original PDF governs all numbers, arcs, dot layouts and diagrams; no every-character proofread of optional rules or complete printable playing set is certified. SOURCE INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES preserved: movement-cost tables on pages9and44 show7MP to engage hand-to-hand, while the detailed page14 rule says5MP. SideShow page36 deployment directions appear inconsistent with its victory-table travel directions. RaceAgainstTime page39 says turn5reinforcements enter from the north in Deployment but any side in SpecialRules. No missing official errata or house resolution is invented. Physical22x34maps and counter sheets remain required; small scenario map diagrams and templates are not claimed as full-size replacements. One specific MAJOR activation-order finding is recorded, separately from these unresolved source ambiguities; no full summary audit, PASS or body repair.

attempts.title: Co-opoly: The Game of Cooperatives — MIT-hosted BCDI draft curriculum rules account plus separately labelled UGA2017 participant handout
attempts.selection_note: Usable combined written Co-opoly rules reference: the Economic Democracy Training Curriculum draft hosted by MIT CoLab, Workshop7 Worker Cooperatives, PDF149–150, explicitly names Co-opoly: The Game of Cooperatives and introduces its account as From the website; separately corroborated by University of Georgia Robert Nick Cochran2017 thesis participant instructions, AppendixC PDF55–56/printed49–50. Unique named game and cooperative-business setup, character income/cost-of-living, shared pawn, four card families, Work challenges, salary12 and starting-second-cooperative victory match Brian Van Slyke/TESA BGG115997. No substitution of Monopoly Deal, the2018 anti-condo Monopoly conversion, or other games using co-opoly as a generic name. Both complete selected game sections were read and their original two-page images visually inspected. Thesis title/author and methods PDF25–26 were read for provenance and scope; unrelated study questionnaires/results and Monopoly appendix are excluded from canonical selection. Reference covers choosing the co-op, random character cards/individual starting balances,20point-per-player co-op deposits in the handout, common pawn/alternating die/space-deck draws, World/Resource/Challenge/Work cards, charades/unspoken/drawing, point bank versus jointly controlled coop funds, mandatory pay-day stops/salary12, end-year cost of living, everyone losing if either the co-op or any player goes bankrupt, and second-co-op Challenge-card victory. The participant handout additionally says cards use the first side seen, transfers occur only at pay-day/end-year spaces and a second-co-op card is completed there. These supplementary rules remain explicitly attributed to the study handout rather than silently certified as exhaustive publisher wording. The MIT document is marked DRAFT and expressly not yet vetted by BCDI partners; it is a third-party curriculum reference, not an original publisher rulebook or a peer-reviewed rules authority. The UGA study uses two-person45minute sessions, rewards, restarting after bankruptcy and trying to start additional co-ops before the timer ends. These are labelled research-protocol additions and not promoted to ordinary game victory or player-count rules. LIMITS: actual original publisher manual remains unrecovered; complete Work-card procedures/timing, all board-printed annual and cost-of-living increments, character balances, decks, board and edition-specific edge cases remain required. The participant handout’s shortened wording around starting a co-op and its restart instructions are preserved without changing the curriculum’s original second-co-op objective. Accurate source type is RULES REFERENCE PDF, not a complete publisher rulebook. Whole unchanged434page curriculum and58page thesis are retained, with canonical text limited to the two matching game sections. No full summary audit, PASS, summary-body repair or verified badge.

attempts.title: Fury in the West: A Commander’s Notebook — Robert D. Harmon; Avalon Hill The General 18-1, May-June 1981; selected rules briefing
attempts.selection_note: Publisher Avalon Hill The General, volume 18 number 1, May-June 1981, Robert D. Harmon, Fury in the West: A Commander’s Notebook. Actual unchanged 50-page magazine PDF retrieved successfully. Cover date/issue native text and original printed page 3 title/byline/publisher preface identify it. The preface explicitly says the Battleline game needed no Avalon Hill revision beyond new map and bookcase packaging, supporting the named Battleline 1977 game rather than a different title. Original images of printed/PDF pages 3, 6, 7 and 9 were visually read. Canonical selected regions contain the publisher preface, full Critical Issue 1 Initial Briefing, Critical Issue 2 Unit Reduction and Critical Issue 3 Rules, ending before Critical Issue 4 Union Organization. Coverage includes brigade forces and leader chains, three scenarios/day-night structure, offboard permanent casualty and recoverable straggler tracks, examples, ordinary movement attrition, columns, elimination when tracks meet, flank/rear doubling, two units per hex, frontal-three-hex ZOC/mandatory combat/withdrawal, facing costs, advanced artillery/night/reorganization, explicitly optional initiative/cavalry/stacking/leader/other variants, and scenario-specific victory points. Normal day-one Confederate/day-two Union initiative is distinct from the optional die-roll initiative rule. Day-one Pittsburgh Landing and day-two Shiloh Church bonuses are distinguished from the two-day scenario, which lacks special territorial objectives. This is an accurately labelled publisher-magazine RULES REFERENCE PDF, not the complete original rulebook. Exact scenario starting hexes, full terrain/movement costs, complete CRT, strength records, all recovery rates/edge cases and original physical components remain missing. Native text has old OCR spelling/hyphenation artifacts; source page images govern exact wording and numbers. Regions preserve original column order and stop before unrelated organization/strategy sections. The later author-proposed alternative setups, victory conditions and new optional rules on pages 12–13 are excluded. Printed Optional Rules on page 9 remain explicitly optional, including recommendations/commentary. The earlier volume18number5 PDF has only a product advertisement and is held, not accepted as the rules feature. Grognard’s user-inferred leader elimination erratum is not promoted into official rules. One specific source-backed MAJOR finding records omitted mandatory ordinary-movement straggler losses; no full summary audit, PASS or body repair.

attempts.selection_note: Detailed German Cliquenabend rules account for Noris’s 2008 Europa-Wissen by Arno Steinwender and Christoph Puhl, successfully retrieved unchanged from its actual public game page. This is the named Im Fadenkreuz: Europa, BGG 37730: cached primary BGG metadata explicitly lists Europa-Wissen as its alternate name, and authors/year/publisher plus rings/map/coordinate-string mechanism match. No ID change or substitution of 2009 Deutschland-Wissen, the unrelated Kosmos Europa quiz, or political/military games. The complete selected Ziel des Spiels, Spielaufbau and Spielablauf sections were read, ending before the separate Strategie/opinion section. An independently retrieved Reich der Spiele review dated 2 September 2008 corroborates the same game, authors, 110 double-sided question cards and coordinate-string/ring solution mechanism. Account supplies string threading, central map, three differently sized coloured rings and score marker per player, 110 cards/220 questions, starter’s die and rotation, die-selected ordinary/speed/double-points rounds, choosing/reading/showing the picture question, sequential normal ring placement with overlap allowed, coordinate-string answer reveal, 2/3/5 points for large/medium/small rings containing the correct intersection, zero for misses, country-question small-ring/two-point plus opponent-miss bonuses, no repositioning, simultaneous speed placement with extra points for correct rings covered by later rings, double scoring and score-threshold ending. Accurate source is a THIRD-PARTY RULES REFERENCE HTML in original German, not an English translation or recovered publisher manual. The reviewer’s parenthesized suggestion to always use the top question is explicitly commentary, retained and not silently promoted to an official rule. Important original inconsistency: the goal section says 30 points or more ends play; the final sentence says more than30 points. Both are preserved verbatim, and the exact threshold boundary is not resolved or invented. Full first-player selection, simultaneous threshold/tie handling, every country/die interaction and all publisher edge cases are not independently established. The actual coordinate map, question/answer cards, die and rings remain necessary; the complete question deck is not reproduced. The official current Noris manual archive was separately checked through all three advertised pages and its exact-product public search. No matching Europa/606104536 manual link appears; a bounded historical index for that rules subdomain also yielded no matching record. This is limited discovery, not proof no original manual exists. Canonical selected HTML text normalizes whitespace only and excludes navigation, later strategy/reviews and unrelated games; unchanged main/supporting HTML retain hashes. Linked WMV was not needed or executed. One specific MAJOR deck-exhaustion ending finding is recorded; the source’s own threshold ambiguity remains explicit. No full publisher-rulebook audit, PASS or summary-body repair.

games.title: Jinsei Game

attempts.title: 人生ゲーム — タカラトミー 2008年 第6代; original Japanese eight-page manual
attempts.selection_note: Complete unchanged eight-page original Japanese Takara Tomy Jinsei Game manual, copyright 1968/2008, product JAN 4904810301912, downloaded directly from the publisher support archive. The publisher product page independently identifies this as the sixth edition, released August 2008, with Junior and Millionaire stages and combined play. This is the named Japanese Jinsei Game family, BGG 145428, and its Junior childhood/school-to-career stage matches the local description; no Western LIFE manual or themed Adventure/MOVE/Jumbo Dream substitute is used. Accepted scope is explicitly the 2008 sixth edition, not a facsimile or certification of every edition since 1968. All eight original page images were visually inspected. The manual contains components, physical setup, banker/turn order/initial money, Junior movement and allowance spaces, mandatory STOPs and school-trip branches, borrowing and careers, Junior finish/scoring, Millionaire setup/movement/paydays, marriage/branch/settlement STOPs, debt and repayment, career changes/rank-ups, insurance, stocks, treasure cards, marriage/children, house purchase/exchange, gambling/revenge, settlement, finish/final asset valuation and combined-stage carryover. Native PDF text is severely corrupted and was not used. Fresh forced Japanese OCR was run separately over all eight pages using locally downloaded Japanese language data. The Japanese-only OCR remains imperfect, including numbers, furigana, columns, card names and diagram labels. Clearly labelled short visually checked Japanese readings accompany the raw OCR; the unchanged original PDF governs every numerical value and diagram. This is an original Japanese source, not an official or machine-generated English translation. The printed board, cards, spinner and physical components remain necessary; their full faces are not recreated by the manual. One specific MAJOR finding is recorded for the covered 2008 scoring/component scope: the summary substitutes hidden-value LIFE tiles for the original treasure-card and final-asset system. No full summary audit, PASS or body repair.

games.title: Mega-Mania

attempts.title: Block Mania / Mega-Mania — Esoteric Order of Gamers reference v1.1 (December2021), with selected Italian translation comparison
attempts.selection_note: Complete unchanged eight-page English Esoteric Order of Gamers / Peter Universal Head Gifford Block Mania reference, v1.1 December2021, explicitly identifying Games Workshop1987 and including Mega-Mania. Operative PDF pages4-8 were read; original pages5 and8 visually checked. Pages1-3 are cover/promotion/attribution; pages6-8 print two identical copies, so only each left half is selected after exact text equality checks. Covers base setup and counters, command/deployment/activation/movement, defensive fire, attacks, fire/collapse, special units/equipment/locations, Mania and Justice effects, endgame and defeat-point ranking. Page8 supplies the missing expansion-specific 3/4-player setup: remove12/6cards, shared hardware/armoury pools, turn/board order, wraparound movement and shooting, skyrail/mega-way/flying access, multiplayer defensive fire and four-Klegg limit. A separately attributed Italian Goblin2002 translation is retained unchanged as a comparison component; selected section3 on PDF pages3-4 and section12 on PDF page11 independently corroborate setup counts and continuing Justice endgame. PDF page11 visually checked. The actual current publisher product page confirms Richard Halliwell, two additional block boards, up to four players and separate Happy Hour bundling; its inspected public links contain no rule download. Earlier publisher URL redirects to a collection, not a manual. This is a usable third-party reference, not a verified original rulebook or an authoritative correction of all rules. The English reference visibly repeats pedway text under its base Mega-way heading, omits the structural-damage defeat-point entry found in the Italian translation, and has apparent copied/garbled bat-suit and demo-charge wording. The Italian translation also combines base and expansion rules and does not include the separately referenced Blockers Manual. Differences in detailed scoring, combat order and movement wording are not silently reconciled. Original publisher rules should govern these details. The selected Italian setup/endgame text is separately attributed and retained in its original language, not presented as English or official translation. The optional, explicitly untested more-than-four-player MEGA MEGA-MANIA section is excluded. Happy Hour is a separate expansion bundled in the current reprint, not the named 1987 Mega-Mania scope; no Happy Hour coverage is claimed. Both references explicitly agree that Mania-deck exhaustion STARTS the Justice stage and play continues until the last blocker is removed or all blocks collapse. This supports a specific summary MAJOR finding only; no full summary audit, PASS, source-error adjudication or summary-body repair.

games.title: Minion Hunter

attempts.title: Minion Hunter — GDW/FFE public six-page sample, original printed2–5 only; scoped rules reference
attempts.selection_note: Actual six-page public publisher/DriveThruRPG sample 60396-sample.pdf successfully retrieved unchanged. Original title, GDW/FFE marks, 1992 copyright and Lester Smith credits match the named Minion Hunter Dark Conspiracy boardgame. All six original sample pages were visually read and freshly forced English OCRed because the existing native layer is badly garbled and interleaves columns. PDF1 is contents; PDF2 is rules-file cover; PDF3–6 reproduce original printed pages2–5. They supply introduction/components, setup with no initial money, twelve unexamined Plot Cards removed, one initial point in each attribute, highest D10 first/clockwise, first-turn off-board corner choice and Security Training correction to +2 Combat, location-dependent player turns, exact D6 career movement either direction, corner-to-map choice, map travel/declared vehicle and public-transport costs/encounter interruption, hospital recovery, after-each-player Plot Card movement/reveal and replacement timing, and initial attribute definitions. This is a usable scoped RULES_REFERENCE_PDF, not the full original manual or full game download. The sample ends mid Gaining Attribute Points on printed5. Remaining attributes/testing, equipment, complete Plot Card effects, combat, encounter/transport tables, victory/endings, Grimmer Options and maps/cards/pawns/money are unavailable in this sample. The file cover advertises nine rule pages including Grimmer Options while the original component description calls the core book eight pages; these distinct descriptions are preserved. Contents lists Minion Nation in the full paid bundle, but no expansion rules are present in this six-page sample or merged into base rules. Sample-file watermark remains unchanged and causes OCR losses; images govern all obscured wording, numbers and diagrams. The paid store GET returned403 and was not bypassed. A different Scribd upload exposes no ordinary current readable rule text; its cached text and purchaser metadata are excluded. No purchase, login or restricted download. One specific MAJOR turn-order finding is supported by original printed3and5; no full summary audit, PASS or summary body repair.

attempts.title: Rare Species — complete BGG community rules account, actual 23 June 2021 public HTML capture
attempts.selection_note: Complete detailed English community rules account for Spear’s David Bellamy Rare Species, BGG 18143, recovered unchanged within the publicly archived BGG HTML page captured 23 June 2021. The requested older archive URL redirected to that actual 2021 capture, which is recorded explicitly; this is not described as a 2010 document. The original public HTML embeds its published description as JSON in GEEK.geekitemPreload.item.description. It was decoded statically with json.JSONDecoder and the description HTML parsed as text; no JavaScript or game code was executed. The complete 3,196-character description matches the independently cached current public BGG item description exactly. It is a substantive community rules reference, not just catalogue metadata or automatically generated prose. Matching original booklet-cover and Conservation Park photographs were individually viewed; the title, David Bellamy endorsement, sex-coloured card backs and three bamboo holding spaces corroborate identity and the cage component. Account covers 2–4 players, main board/four parks/four pawns/24 cards, twelve hidden females on yellow spaces and twelve exposed males on green spaces, corner-track starts, clockwise die movement, first-stage successful female capture with male remaining on board, maximum three unpaired females in holding cages, later identification of a caged mate to claim a completed breeding pair, failed flips, stealing unpaired females from opponents and releasing one own female on a failed theft, no shared pawn spaces, skipping positions whose male was already claimed, all-females-paired ending and most completed pairs victory. Accurate source type is THIRD-PARTY COMMUNITY RULES REFERENCE HTML, not the recovered original publisher manual, a certified transcription or proof of every German/English edition. First-player selection, full-cage/occupied-space edge cases and a tiebreak are not fully specified; no missing rules were invented. The physical board, parks and complete animal-card set remain necessary. Booklet photo is only a cover, and the full original Little Red Data Book/instruction pages remain unrecovered. Selected canonical text contains only the published description, with source wording intact and HTML entities decoded; navigation, scripts and unrelated page metadata are excluded. Unchanged archived HTML and two original photos are retained with hashes. One specific MAJOR two-stage-pairing finding is recorded against the community reference, supported by the original three-cage board; no complete publisher-rulebook audit, PASS or summary-body repair.

games.title: Rave

attempts.title: Rave — original WOW Enterprises 1991 rulebook images; local eight-image convenience PDF
attempts.selection_note: Original WOW Enterprises Ltd 1991 Rave rulebook recovered as eight unchanged linked JPEG scans from actual successful April 2007 public archive captures of the Fantazia gallery. Original title, WOW logo, copyright 1991, publisher credits, distinctive Trip City/M25, flyers, Vibe/Dance cards, energy tokens and triptych mechanisms match named BGG 12645. All eight original images were visually inspected. Core play runs continuously through introduction/components, setup, Quick Edit points 1-10, Fast & Furious stages 1-2, movement/rumours/dealing/money/police/cancellation/gamble and Dance Mix stage 3, card-pair example, winning and losing. Core setup/turn/movement/rumour/dealing/dancing/ending passages were visually read; decorative cover/symbols, glossary and tiny credits were identified rather than exhaustively proofread. Source has three distinguished versions: Quick Edit introduction, Fast & Furious race-to-rave with sufficient energy, and Dance/Tuff Mix collecting three matching triptych pieces. The booklet itself varies wording around arrival energy: Quick Edit explicitly says minimum five then grants a free token; a detailed stage-2 introduction mentions six, while later detailed passages again specify five. Those original passages are retained without silently harmonizing them. Source type is original RULEBOOK IMAGES, not a publisher PDF or the small Hyperreal cover thumbnail. The staged PDF is only a local eight-image convenience assembly; all unchanged JPEGs, actual capture URLs, dimensions and SHA-256 hashes are retained separately, plus the unchanged linking gallery HTML. Fresh English OCR covers all eight images. OCR is poor for the decorative symbol page, some glossary/credits, typography and embedded card text; it even misreads the win count and copyright. Explicit visually checked readings precede the raw OCR; the unchanged original images govern exact wording, values, symbols and diagrams. Canonical OCR does not reconstruct the complete board, all A-Z location cards, full Vibe/Dance/flyer decks, tokens or cassette/audio; those physical components remain required. The glossary spread has cropped/overlapping header edges and some tiny credits are difficult to read; no every-character facsimile or complete playable print-and-play set is certified. Initial image requests suffered transient connection errors; bounded retries successfully retrieved all eight rules images. Live Fantazia path returned 404, Hyperreal HTTPS failed TLS while ordinary public HTTP worked but offered only a tiny rulebook cover; author profile had no rules. One specific MAJOR Vibe-card timing finding is recorded; no full summary audit, PASS or body repair.

attempts.title: Ringel-Rangel — Hendrik Cornilly unofficial Dutch translation
attempts.selection_note: Complete two-page Dutch freely translated rules by Hendrik Cornilly, Spelgroep Hof van Watervliet, dated 29 March 2001 and hosted by Vlaams Spellenarchief/Spellenlab. Explicit unofficial translation of Geni Wyss HABA 1993 Ringel-Rangel, matching BGG 10509 wooden turtle/ring dexterity game. Both pages fully read: 24 turtles/20 balls, player color and two shared turtle piles, optional zero-to-three branches, matching entry/goal, one-finger push and legal board support, fallen-piece penalty collection, neutral own-color balls, error-free return of a ball, end after both piles exhausted and fewest penalties wins. Native text intact. Matching original French last page independently confirms penalty-based ending, but its archived PDF includes an unrelated opening page, so that earlier incomplete original remains unaccepted as main rules. Translation authority is unofficial; the Dutch account describes an extra penalty turtle from an opponents personal supply while French says from the board, so that specific transfer procedure is not certified. Useful full translated source with explicit limitation, not a publisher original or full accuracy audit. Summary opposite victory condition recorded separately.
